preamble: Backing and spirantization of the voiced velar [ɡ] to the voiced uvular fricative [ʁ]. In Amdo Tibetan lects the Old Tibetan preinitial g- (and d-) surfaces as a uvular fricative, and in Uzbek the Proto-Turkic velar in back-vowel words is reflected by gʻ [ʁ], as in togʻ 'mountain' < *tāg.

examples.from: Old Tibetan preinitial g-, e.g. glu 'song', g.yag 'yak'
examples.to: uvular fricative preinitial (Sertha adds an epenthetic schwa after it)
examples.note: Gates (2023) compares Amdo and Gyalrongic reflexes of Old Tibetan g-/d- and weighs a regular sound change g-/d- > uvular fricatives against inheritance and Qiangic/Mongolic contact.
Uzbek gʻ is the voiced uvular fricative /ʁ/; Turkish dağ and Kazakh/Tatar тау show other reflexes of the same final velar.

sources: Gates, J. P. (2023). The uvularization of g-/d- in Tibetic languages. Journal of Language Relationship 21(3–4): 245–258. https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/the-uvularization-of-g-din-tibetic-languages
